mechanism_narrative: Current low and declining RETAIL_REC, coupled with low WORKPLACES and TRANSIT, indicates a persistent trend of reduced discretionary activity, leading to further declines in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days, despite WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remaining low.

mechanism_narrative: The sustained low level of WORKPLACES mobility, remaining below -30% for four consecutive weeks and flat at -34.9%, suggests a continued absence from offices, which will suppress RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks as fewer people are in commercial areas.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains below -30% for 4 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: WORKPLACES mobility rises above -30% within the next two weeks, and RETAIL_REC increases.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated RESIDENTIAL mobility combined with declining GROCERY_PHARM mobility suggests people are staying home more but reducing their essential outings, indicating a general reduction in all out-of-home activities, which will negatively impact RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility falls below baseline while GROCERY_PHARM mobility stabilizes or increases, and RETAIL_REC rises.

mechanism_narrative: The recent drop in PARKS mobility from its peak (22.4% to 15.9%), combined with the current date (mid-August), suggests the tail end of peak summer outdoor activity, which will lead to a slight rebound in indoor retail as weather becomes less favorable, boosting RETAIL_REC over the next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility drops by more than 5 points week-on-week in mid-August
failure_condition: PARKS mobility continues to decline or remains low, and RETAIL_REC does not show an increase in the next week.

mechanism_narrative: The recent sharp decline in TRANSIT mobility (from -26.9% to -29.7% week-on-week) indicates a reduction in travel for all purposes, directly correlating with lower footfall in retail areas and thus driving RETAIL_REC down over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT mobility falls by more than 2 points week-on-week
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility stabilizes or increases in the next two weeks, and RETAIL_REC does not decline.

mechanism_narrative: The combined sustained low levels of WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility, both hovering around -30% below baseline, indicate a significant reduction in daily commuting and associated city-center activity, which will continue to depress RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: Either WORKPLACES or TRANSIT mobility shows a sustained increase of more than 5 points, and RETAIL_REC rises.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent week-on-week decline in GROCERY_PHARM mobility, reaching -8.6%, suggests a broader trend of reduced essential outings, which will likely extend to discretionary spending, causing RETAIL_REC to decline over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM mobility stabilizes or increases, and RETAIL_REC does not decline.

mechanism_narrative: While RESIDENTIAL mobility is currently elevated, the approaching end of summer holidays (late August/early September) will likely see a return to routine, causing RESIDENTIAL to fall and RETAIL_REC to increase as people resume out-of-home activities over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility remains elevated or increases further, and RETAIL_REC does not show an increase.
